newsitem.title: USA: Mobile Tel amends $250 mln credit line.
newsitem.headline: Mobile Tel amends $250 mln credit line.

text.p: Mobile Telecommunication Technologies Corp said on Thursday it agreed to amend its $250 million revolving credit facility to reflect slower than expected subscriber growth.
Mobile Telecommunication said the amendments centered the bank covenants for subscriber growth and cash flow to match the company's three-year business plan.
When the company originally took out the loans in December 1995, the company anticipated the number of subscribers to be higher than it currently is.

Mobile Telecommunication said it had about 1.3 million paging and messaging unit in service at the end of 1996, including about 30,000 narrowband personal communications services (PCS) customers. The company said the total of units in service increased by 26 percent from 1995 totals.
The company's bank covenant originally called for 100,000 narrowband PCS customers at this time, said Scott Hamilton, director of investor relations.
Hamilton said Mobile Telecommunications has not changed its longer term outlook, including the addition of 200,000 narrowband PCS customers by the end of 1997.
